correctness.rationale: The ordinary matching complex is the independence complex of the Heawood line graph, not its perfect-matching extendibility subcomplex. A clean-room exact enumeration generated the 168 point permutations preserving the Fano lines and adjoined a polarity, giving the full 336 permutations since the connected incidence graph has a unique bipartition. The chain vertices of a barycentric simplex have different ranks, so stabilizers fix the simplex pointwise, and no two distinct vertices of a simplex become identified in the quotient. Rank order therefore gives the alternating integral orbit-flag boundary with no orientation sign from transport. The independent enumeration reproduced face counts (21,168,644,1218,1050,336,24), orbit-cell counts (29,311,1400,3051,3375,1800,360), and all boundary-square identities. Exact integer unit pivots (28,283,1117,1934,1440,360) give a chain-homotopy reduction to Z in degrees 0 and 4, with zero differential, so there is no undetected torsion. The original one-skeleton's spanning tree leaves 148 generators; triangle relators eliminate all in waves (96,38,14). The 21 stabilizers of single-edge matchings, each of order 16, generate all 336 elements, so Armstrong's theorem applies to the simply connected finite complex and gives trivial quotient fundamental group. Successive Hurewicz applications and homological Whitehead then give the asserted homotopy equivalence, not a homeomorphism. The supplied verifier was inspected, not executed. Replay the independent exhaustive calculation with python3 /workspace/branches/92ea9803-fefc-4d67-bf7c-764eb65c1c11/recompute_heawood.py; its adjacent log records the results. The script does not formalize Armstrong or Hurewicz–Whitehead.

value.rationale: The full symmetry quotient is natural for this canonical incidence graph, and the known rational invariant line motivates asking whether it is actually an integral homotopy sphere. Both potential obstructions, torsion and nontrivial fundamental group, are settled at once. This is an independently useful complete classification for the fixed object, without claiming a family result or a homeomorphism theorem.
